title: Connected numerical MultiRange not hiding unfilterable values correctly

comments.body:
Looking at a way around this it looks like it wouldn't be possible to use the `data/values` provided by Algolia since it doesn't return all the possible values for numericAttributes:

```json
{
    "name":"startTimeEpoch",
    "data": {
        "1489581000":139,
        "1489581060":138,
        "1489581120":143,
        "1489581180":146,
        "1489581240":136,
        "1489581300":120,
        "1489581360":129,
        "1489581420":114,
        "1489581480":86,
        "1489581540":38,
        "1489585500":28,
        "1489589400":38,
        "1489722600":28,
        "1489788000":153,
        "1490997600":92,
        "1491606000":141,
        "1492250400":111,
        "1506124800":82,
        "1509145200":51,
        "1510009200":80
    },
    "exhaustive":true,
    "stats": {
        "min":1489543740,
        "max":1510009200,
        "avg":1490079779,
        "sum":17624663633760
    }
}
```

Since the list there is not an exact list containing every single `startTimeEpoch` in the index, I cannot use that to provide a more accurate list of days that are used.

Hi @RyanTheAllmighty,

You're right, the `noRefinement` feature of the MultiRange was done with a different logic that the one you need. 

While we are thinking about this issue, maybe you can try those following workaround:

1. You can create your own connector by reusing the MultiRange one, and just changing the logic.
2. Maybe you could use the RefinementList instead. The RefinementList has a prop `transformItems` that can let you return an array that will contain days. And by increasing the limitMin, you can check if you have some date that falls in. 

What do you think?

@mthuret I didn't even think about creating a custom connector, I'll give that a shot now and see how it goes and report back, but I think the issue I mentioned in my second comment, about the API not returning a full list of possible values in the `numericAtributes` response, but I'll do some digging.

Yeah unfortunately as per my second comment, Algolia only provides 20 values which when there is a large amount of results will miss some days so this approach is not practical unfortunately.

Any other ideas on how to achieve this?
@RyanTheAllmighty: did you try to use the refinementList along with `transformItems`?
@RyanTheAllmighty, can you share with us the code you use, that way, we can have a look at it? :)
